question.text: The number of numbers, lying between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>99</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> that can be made from the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> when the digits occur only once in each number, is

solution.text:
Required number of numbers =6P3−5​P2=120−20=100.

{Since, between 99 & 1000, the numbers are of 3 digits, but those numbers should be omitted in which 0 comes at hundreds place}.
